class: a witness written as a ground

expect.why: the second ground is the witness: the digest of the Observation section as it stood before the lift took prose out of it. `freshness` reads grounds, compares that anchor against the tree, and finds a section that no longer digests to it — on this run and on every run after it, because the lift is what made the two differ and nothing will ever put the prose back

the flag is true and the entry is not wrong about anything: the prose is held, the witness resolves, and the measurement the claim rests on is still in the section. What is wrong is where the provenance was written. A witness belongs on the `lifted:` line of the passage, which `freshness` does not read; written as a ground it is a standing flag no reading verdict can honestly clear, since a reading anchored to the section as it stands now is a reading of text the witness was never about

note: the negative of the rule `check_passages` states by refusing a witness stated by reference: a witness names an artifact as it stood before the lift, and every checker that reads grounds is asking about the artifact as it stands now. Ground 1 is the same section anchored where it actually is and passes, which is what keeps the flag on ground 2 from reading as a complaint about the lift itself. That `freshness` says nothing about the `lifted:` line carrying the very same digest is the other half of the seed: a passage is not a ground, and the corpus would show it if it ever became one.
history: apply commits/01, commits/02, … as successive commits in a fresh repository; expectations name the commit they apply to. `@commitNN` in an entry is substituted with the real short object id of that commit before it is made, because a seed cannot know an id the runner has not created yet
